pages.title: What is Emergent?
pages.brief: Emergent is an agentic vibecoding platform: you describe what you want, and AI agents build, test, and deploy it. Positioning vs traditional coding.

pages.title: What kind of apps you can build?
pages.brief: Full-stack web apps, mobile apps, landing pages, MVPs, dashboards, internal tools, e-commerce - projects of any scale.

children.title: For Individuals
children.brief: Personal apps, trackers, portfolios, side projects.

children.title: For Small & Medium Businesses
children.brief: Internal tools, dashboards, customer-facing apps.

children.title: For Enterprises
children.brief: Complex multi-user platforms at scale.

pages.title: The chat-to-deployment flow
pages.brief: The big-picture arc of building on Emergent: prompt -> build -> preview -> iterate -> deploy. A map of the whole journey before diving in.

pages.title: A tour of the workspace
pages.brief:
1. Chat panel: where you talk to the agent.
2. Preview panel: live view of your app; auto-updates.
3. Secrets / env area: where API keys & env vars live (separate from deployment).
4. GitHub controls: where save/pull lives.
5. Deploy controls: where deploy/redeploy/replace live.
6. Uploading files/images to the agent: attach a screenshot, design, or CSV as build input.

pages.title: Which prompt window should I use?

2. Quick decision guide: a short 'if you want X, pick Y' chooser before the comparison table.

pages.title: Compare the 4 windows
pages.brief:
1. SINGLE TABLE PAGE. Columns = Fullstack Builder / Mobile App / Landing Page / Brainstorm; Rows = What it's for / What it CAN do / What it CAN'T do / Pick it when.
2. Key mobile note: a native Mobile App runs on a different language/stack underneath - NOT a web URL in a wrapper (drives later domain/bundle-ID/publication behaviour).

pages.title: Your first build (walkthrough)
pages.brief:
1. Pick a simple idea (e.g. book tracker); keep it small.
2. Write the first prompt: purpose + features + design hint + UX hint.
3. Answer the agent's clarifying questions: Universal Key vs own key, auth?, design prefs, start-vs-discuss.
4. Watch it build: real-time steps; ~5-15 min; read the explanations.

children.title: Prompting basics
children.brief:
1. Be specific and detailed: the agent rewards clarity.
2. Concise features beat mega-prompts: lowers credit burn and confusion.
3. Ask the agent to explain before building: 'explain, don't build yet'.
4. Why pasting a ChatGPT plan underperforms: an external spec often doesn't map to Emergent's flow.

children.brief: Preview and deployed apps use SEPARATE databases; data does not auto-flow between them - a common gotcha.

children.brief: Redeploy keeps the existing production DB; replace can take a fresh prod DB (from preview) or keep the existing one.

children.brief: Add a new env var for your DB; a background process migrates from Emergent DB to yours; app keeps running.

pages.title: File storage (Emergent Object Store)
pages.brief: S3-compatible file storage powered by Tigris (5GB/org quota, no AWS account) for user uploads; requested via the agent, and storage operations do not consume credits.

pages.title: Scheduled tasks & background jobs in your app
pages.brief: In-process schedulers (APScheduler/Celery/threading) can silently die under scale-to-zero on lower tiers; use external cron trigger endpoints, an always-on tier, or decoupled async workers.

children.title: What is Expo?
children.brief: Expo is the framework/toolchain behind Emergent mobile apps. Expo Go is a free phone app: scan a QR code and your app runs live on your device - no APK or store publish needed to test.

children.brief:

2. Answer clarifying questions.
3. Preview live on your phone via Expo Go (scan QR).
4. Iterate/debug with the agent.
5. When ready, move to publishing.

children.title: Signing & keystore
children.brief: Google Play needs a signed .aab; you generate a keystore that is your app's identity. Once published with a keystore, every future update must use the SAME one. Losing the keystore means you can NEVER update the app - store it in two secure places; consider Google Play App Signing as backup.
